node.title: Re^7: Two meanings of undef
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
The statement if( defined(X) ){say 'defined';} else {say 'not defined';} is syntactically invalid but Perl interpreter does not recognizes as such due to problem with syntax analysis in interpreter (which sometimes accept clearly syntactically incorrect statements as syntactically valid.

No, it's valid syntax because X could be a function, or a bareword under no strict 'subs'. Update: Taken as a single snippet, there is not enough context to tell if the compiler will reject it or not. In [AnomalousMonk]'s example above it's valid because there is no use strict.
